finding: Non-Goal 6 defers a deliverable on a premise §2 falsifies four paragraphs earlier, and the shipped surface agrees with §2. Non-Goal 6: 'Under `blocking`, a clean round can have surviving `warning` and `info` rows and **tp emits no count of them**, so an agent reading `clean: true` cannot tell an empty round from a suppressed one.' §2's boundary paragraph says the opposite in terms: '`role_streaks[].open` ... computed by `auditRoundOpenByRole` (`engine/rolestreaks.go:128-142`) through `AuditRowIsPass` alone. Under `blocking` a round can therefore record `clean: true` beside a **non-zero `open`** — correct rather than defective: `open` counts findings, `clean` answers whether the phase may end.' Verified in the shipped surface rather than inferred: `skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:758-796` documents `role_streaks` as emitted on `tp audit <spec> --status` (with or without `--check`) and on `tp audit <spec> --record <file>`, each entry `{role, consecutive_clean, open}`, and `internal/cli/audit_record.go:152` sets it unconditionally as an always-emitted array. So under `blocking` an agent reading `clean: true` sees `role_streaks` and the sum of `open` over it is exactly the count of suppressed rows: zero for an empty round, non-zero for a suppressed one. The two cases are distinguishable today, in JSON, without reading round files. What is genuinely missing is the *severity breakdown* — how many of the surviving rows are `warning` versus `info` — which is a much smaller deferral than 'no count' and does not support Non-Goal 6's closing instruction ('an operator setting `blocking` reads the round files for what was suppressed'), since `--status` already answers how many. This matters beyond wording: the false premise is being handed forward — `spec/0.46.0.md` §8.3 receives this non-goal, so the spec that is supposed to build the counterpart will start from a claim that tp emits nothing.
suggestion: Restate Non-Goal 6 on the true gap: 'Under `blocking`, a clean round can carry surviving `warning` and `info` rows. Their *count* is already observable — `role_streaks[].open` stays severity-blind by §2's boundary, so a non-zero `open` beside `clean: true` is exactly the suppressed population — but their *severity breakdown* is not, and `nonblocking_open`'s review-side shape is what would give it. Creating the counterpart means inverting a pinned guard, which this release does not do.' Delete 'reads the round files for what was suppressed' and put `role_streaks[].open` there instead. Correct `spec/0.46.0.md` §8.3 in the same edit, since it already carries the inherited version of this claim.

finding: The fence paragraph was rewritten in this batch and the rewrite built a cost estimate on a premise the source refutes. finding: The fence's trigger is specified for exactly one of the field's two values, and the two readings are not equivalent. §2 names 'tp set --workflow audit_converge_on=blocking' and its --project form; §5 test 9 asserts those two commands exit 2 under TP_UNATTENDED=1 and 0 without it. Both answers are defensible and the spec picks neither: refuse every write of the field (simple, and it means a unit cannot restore the strict value either), or refuse only the relaxing value, mirroring the cap fence, which by engine.UnattendedRaise accepts an equal-or-lower value precisely because 'lowering a budget cannot manufacture convergence' (internal/engine/unattended.go:70-73). finding: §2 bans a word in the sentence immediately below the table that uses it, and the banned word is in the normative definition of one of the two values. finding: §2 promises the twin's validation behaviour and names none of the sinks that deliver it, and the missing half is the one that decides what happens when the gate predicate is handed a value it cannot grade. review_converge_on validates in FOUR places, two per exit code: set.go:375 and set_project.go:68 reject a bad literal argument as a usage error (exit 2), and review_status.go:39 and review_record.go:48 reject an invalid RESOLVED value from a stored layer as a validation error (exit 1), each with engine.ReviewConvergeOnHint. §2 states only 'rejected with the same hint machinery when the value is neither', and §5 test 2 only 'an invalid value is refused with the same hint shape review_converge_on uses' — no exit code, no command. An invalid resolved value reaching tp audit <spec> --record or tp audit <spec> --status is a validation error (exit 1) with the same hint, mirroring review_status.go:39 and review_record.go:48; an unrecognised resolved value is never treated as a policy.' finding: §2 says the fence does not fit a string field and then costs the widening as two new call sites, and the two statements cannot both be acted on. fenceWorkflowWrite(field string, requested float64) is numeric through its whole body, not only in its signature (internal/cli/unattended.go:56-82): engine.FencedCapField gates entry and returns silently at :64-66 for an unfenced field, engine.ResolvedCapValue returns a float, engine.UnattendedRaise is a numeric comparison, and refuseUnattended composes the message setting %s to %s above the resolved %s through formatCapValue. A string field routed through that path either produces no refusal at all or produces the message setting audit_converge_on to blocking above the resolved all. So the release needs a new membership predicate and a new message, not two call sites - and §5 pins neither, because test 9 asserts exit codes only and is green over a refusal whose hint says above the resolved.
suggestion: Cost it as what it is: a string-valued fence helper beside fenceWorkflowWrite, a membership predicate in place of UnattendedRaise, and a refusal message with no comparison in it. Then extend test 9 past the exit code - the refusal hint on both paths names tp escalate --decision audit-converge-on and contains no comparison word - which is also the assertion that catches the reuse of the cap message.

finding: §2's fence cost — 'Widening it is two new call sites in two files' — omits the two edits without which those call sites do nothing, and the omission fails silently in the direction of an unfenced field. fenceWorkflowWrite (internal/cli/unattended.go:56-76) returns early unless engine.FencedCapField(field) is true, and that predicate is backed by var fencedCapFields (internal/engine/unattended.go:46-54), a fixed map of seven numeric fields. It then reads engine.ResolvedCapValue(&wf, field) — a switch over those same seven, returning (float64, bool) — and engine.UnattendedRaise(field, requested, resolved), whose whole semantics is an ordinal comparison. So a string branch that calls fenceWorkflowWrite("audit_converge_on", ???) has no float to pass, and if it passes one anyway the call returns at the FencedCapField guard as a no-op: the field ships documented as fenced and is not. The real change is (a) a fenced-set entry or a second predicate, (b) a non-ordinal refusal path, and only then (c) the two call sites. One consequence to decide with it: engine/unattended_test.go:69 asserts FencedCapField("review_clean_rounds") is false, commented 'a convergence count is not a budget' — adding a convergence-policy field to fencedCapFields contradicts that shipped assertion's stated rationale, so the fenced set is probably the wrong home.

Then §5 test 9's failing arm is real: an implementation that reuses fenceWorkflowWrite unchanged exits 0 under TP_UNATTENDED and the test reddens.

finding: §2.1's second row measures a cycle that has not finished, and §5 test 8 freezes that unfinished history into testdata under a rationale that rules out exactly this. §2.1: '| v0.36.0 | **13, never converged** | round 3 (r2, r3 carry zero `error`) | **never — no round reaches zero** |'. Read from the corpus: `spec/.tp-review/0.36.0/state.json` holds 13 audit rounds, the last recorded 2026-09-01T19:37:28Z with 3 non-`PASS` rows (2 `error`, 1 `warning`) and `clean: false`, and CLAUDE.md's release table lists v0.36.0 as **In flight**. So 'never converged' and 'never — no round reaches zero' are statements about a loop that is still running: a round 14 is expected, and the cycle converging under `all` at rounds 14-15 would falsify both cells. §5 test 8 then pins them — '`blocking` at 3 and `all` never for the second. Both rows are pinned because the v0.36.0 row is the one that argues against the default' — while its own justification for using testdata is 'that is live state **for cycles still in flight**, and an acceptance criterion that moves when unrelated work is recorded is not one.' Copying an in-flight history into `testdata/` does not satisfy that rationale, it evades it: the criterion stops moving but starts being wrong, and it is wrong about the cycle §2.1 calls decisive. Everything else in §2.1 checks out against the corpus — v0.35.0 converges under `blocking` at 3 and under `all` at 9, round 4 carries {error 1, warning 2, info 1}, v0.36.0's rounds 7, 12 and 13 each carry `error`, and the round-3 cell is right for both — which is why the in-flight cells are the only thing to fix.
suggestion: Two options, both honest. (a) Cite the v0.36.0 row as of a stated round and commit — '| v0.36.0 | 13 rounds recorded at <sha>, not converged | round 3 | not by round 13 |' — and make test 8 assert the same bounded claim ('`all` does not converge within the 13 recorded rounds'), which stays true however the cycle ends. (b) Wait for v0.36.0 to close before pinning it, since this release already depends on v0.36.0 shipping elsewhere in the plan. Do not leave 'never' in either the table or the test: it is the one word the cycle can still refute, and it is load-bearing for the default.

finding: §2.2's closing sentence points at the wrong test, and the test it names says the opposite of what §2.2 needs. §2.2: '§5 **test 5** uses a legacy row because it is convenient and real, not because the case is live.' §5 test 5 is '**`warning` is advisory**, tested separately from `info` because `warning` is 158 of the corpus's 360 non-`PASS` rows' — it uses no legacy row and has nothing to do with out-of-enum severities. finding: Pressing round 5's `by_severity` finding with new evidence rather than repeating it, because the round-5 repair corrected the pin count six→four and left the argument's reach untouched. Two facts, both measured. (1) tp's own code has already decided that a relaxed convergence predicate needs one byte distinguishing "clean because empty" from "clean because discounted", and classified that byte as decision-critical: `review_record.go:212` and `review_status.go:103` both read "next_action and nonblocking_open are decision-critical and survive it [--compact]", and `review_record.go:225-227` states "the field's mere presence signals the accepted-open state". `--compact` is tp's strictest AX filter; surviving it is the strongest statement tp makes about a byte. This release copies review's relaxation and declines the byte review calls decision-critical, then bills the operator for it in prose ("reads the round files for what was suppressed") -- an unbounded manual NDJSON read, which is the exact cost P3 exists to remove. (2) The four pins §4 now counts do not reach the cheapest route. All four -- `spec/0.31.0.md` §8.4 and its test 18, `REFERENCE.md:634`, and `reviewconvergeon_clean_test.go:185-205` (`TestReviewNonBlockingOpen_AuditUnaffected`, verified: it asserts only that `audit --record` and `audit --status` never emit the key) -- are about `nonblocking_open` on `--record`/`--status`. **None touches `tp audit --merge`**, which the loop already runs on the same rows in the same round immediately before `--record`, and whose summary at `audit_merge.go:61-86` already loops those rows building `by_status` and `by_role` and already carries a `--compact`-stripped explanatory key (`overlap_report`, `:90-92`). A `by_severity` counter over non-`PASS` rows there is ~6 lines inside an existing loop, no new command, no new flag, no new config, no round-trip, and inverts zero of the four pins. My verdict, asked for plainly: it is in scope -- it is the smallest surface on which this release's only feature is observable at all, and "deferred" here means the release ships a mechanism whose effect no agent can see.
suggestion: Add to §2's scope: `tp audit --merge`'s summary gains `by_severity`, a count of non-`PASS` rows by severity (with the unrecognised bucket §2's fail-closed rule already defines), emitted only when a non-`PASS` row exists and omitted under `--compact` like `overlap_report`; add a §5 test whose killing mutation is a counter that includes `PASS` rows. If it is still to be declined, say so IN Non-Goal 6 and give a reason that reaches `--merge`, because the four-pin reason does not -- and then state what an agent is expected to do with `clean: true` under `blocking`.

finding: Test 8's fixture was widened this round from a projection to the whole corpus, and the widening is ~1.4 MB of committed bytes that no assertion reads. Round 5 asked for "the `(status, severity)` pairs of v0.35.0's nine recorded rounds ... copied into `testdata/`"; round 6 asks for "The rows of v0.35.0's nine recorded rounds and v0.36.0's thirteen, copied into `testdata/`". finding: Test 9 pins both write paths and not the direction, and the fence tp already ships is directional, so two engineers build opposite fences and both pass. finding: The spec cites ten unchanged sites to the line and never names the one line it changes. §2 pins engine/configresolve.go:261, engine/rolestreaks.go:128-142, internal/cli/unattended.go:56, set.go:414/:428, set_project.go:98/:108, escalate.go:41, review_record.go:231 and audit_signal_test.go:472 — every one of them a thing that stays as it is. finding: a014e14 swept spec/0.41.0.md and spec/0.34.0-candidates.md but left both pointing at a §2 paragraph that no longer exists. spec/0.41.0.md:58-59 (Non-Goal 2): 'spec/0.37.0.md §2 carries the reasoning, in the paragraph distinguishing severity from scope.' spec/0.34.0-candidates.md:12: 'Item 1, scope on audit rows, is now deferred a fourth time by spec/0.37.0.md §2 — which separates it from the severity field it had been bundled with, and takes that half.'
